# Linux Observatory

> Independent, unsponsored technical audiovisual observatory for Linux gaming operated by Ediz Iniziel. Tux with telescope. The footage is the evidence. Testing is the product.

Official website: https://linuxobservatory.github.io/
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@LinuxObservatory
Method: Observe -> Instrument -> Record -> Inspect.

## Start here
- [Homepage](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/): project introduction and featured recordings.
- [Beginner introduction](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/start-here/): guide to understanding Linux gaming observations.
- [Observations](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/observations/): recordings and their documented context.
- [Methodology](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/methodology/): observations, controlled comparisons, and diagnostics.
- [Test environment](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/test-environment/): hardware, software, and version context.
- [About](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/about/): project scope and background.

## Technical guides
- [Graphics stack](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/graphics-stack/): Proton, Vulkan and Mesa/RADV.
- [Learning index](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/learn/): educational articles.
- [Frame pacing](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/learn/frame-pacing/): FPS, frame times, and stuttering.
- [MangoHud](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/learn/mangohud/): performance overlay interpretation.
- [RADV](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/learn/radv/): AMD's Vulkan driver in Mesa.
- [Metrics](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/metrics/): understanding performance readings.
- [Extreme resolutions](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/extreme-resolution/): 8K, 16K and 32K workloads.
- [High-resolution field guide](https://linuxobservatory.github.io/learn/extreme-resolution/): virtual resolutions and experimental limits.

## Evidence boundaries
A recording shows what happened in a particular run under stated conditions. It does not by itself establish a repeatable performance comparison or a root cause. Educational simulations are not measured traces. Use the original footage as the primary record, identify missing measurement data, and avoid invented results.
